vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: xiaodi-obsidian-brain-pro
Version: 1.1.0

The skill bundle provides a legitimate utility for syncing WhatsApp/Telegram messages to an Obsidian vault with local semantic search capabilities. The shell scripts (sync.sh, push_to_git.sh) perform standard Git operations to back up notes, and the Python search engine (search_engine.py) uses a local Ollama instance for embeddings. Notably, the system prompts (organizer.txt) include proactive security instructions for the AI agent to redact sensitive information like API keys and passwords before processing, which serves as a defensive measure against accidental data leakage. While the Git scripts use broad commands (git add -A), the behavior is consistent with the stated purpose of the tool.

llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (WhatsApp/Telegram → Obsidian with local Ollama search and Git backup), but several implementation details are inconsistent or under-specified and could lead to unintended data access or exfiltration if not configured carefully.

dimensions.detail: The skill's files and prompts align with the described goals (format-preserving ingestion, local Ollama semantic search, Git backup, and automatic redaction). However some requested accesses extend beyond what the README explicitly describes: the search script defaults to reading ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory (agent memory), which is not called out in the main description and broadens the data surface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime artifacts read/written files under ~/Obsidian and also ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory; they execute git push operations and call an Ollama HTTP endpoint. SKILL.md and prompts instruct automated Git pushes (push_to_git.sh / sync.sh) and executing a local search service. The code expects/uses environment variables (OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OBSIDIAN_DIR, REMOTE_REPO/REMOTE_BRANCH) but those env vars are not declared in the skill metadata—so runtime will implicitly rely on them or on defaults. Reading the OpenClaw memory path is scope expansion that should be explicitly documented and justified.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec (no downloads). That reduces install-time risk. It includes scripts that will be written to disk as part of skill files, but no external archives/unknown URLs are fetched by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars but the code reads several env vars at runtime (OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OLLAMA_MODEL, OBSIDIAN_DIR, REMOTE_REPO, REMOTE_BRANCH). The default OLLAMA_BASE_URL is a LAN IP (http://192.168.3.120:11434), which could cause traffic to that host if not overridden. The scripts and search code access a potentially sensitive path (~/.openclaw/workspace/memory) and will push files to whatever Git remote is configured—these capabilities require explicit, proportional authorization and should be declared.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true. It requests exec, file_read, file_write and memory_search permissions (metadata). Those privileges are coherent for a skill that writes notes, runs git, and does semantic search, but combined they allow automatic reading of local notes and pushing them to a remote if configured—so the user should confirm the git remote and Ollama endpoint before enabling autonomous invocation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement what it claims, but there are a few engineering gaps you should check before installing:

- Confirm where Git pushes will go: the scripts call git push origin <branch>. Make sure your repository remote is set to a private repo you control (and test pushes) to avoid accidental public uploads.
- Verify and override defaults: set OBSIDIAN_DIR, REMOTE_REPO/REMOTE_BRANCH, OLLAMA_BASE_URL and OLLAMA_MODEL explicitly. The default OLLAMA_BASE_URL points to http://192.168.3.120:11434 (a LAN IP) — if you don't intend to use that host, override it to your local Ollama.
- Review the memory read path: search_engine.py includes ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory in its search paths. Decide whether the skill should read agent memory; if not, remove that path or restrict it.
- Test redaction: the prompts implement heuristics (API key length >20, token prefixes like ghp_, sk-) to redact secrets. Those heuristics are helpful but imperfect—run tests with representative secrets to confirm they are reliably removed before any Git push.
- Audit git workflow: the scripts avoid force pushes and hard resets, but ensure your repo remote and branch are correct and that CI/webhooks won’t leak contents.
- Principle of least privilege: because the skill has exec + read/write + memory_search, only enable it if you trust its configuration and the local endpoints it will call. If you need absolute assurance, run it in an isolated environment (separate machine or VM) and confirm all endpoints and remotes before enabling autonomous operation.

If you want, I can produce a concise checklist and a minimal set of environment variable values to safely test this skill in a sandboxed environment.
